### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The most common developmental complication in bacterial meningitis in the pediatric age is hearing loss, followed by mental retardation, residual epilepsy, hydrocephalus, and visual defects. Bacterial meningitis can lead to damage to the auditory nerve causing hearing loss, cognitive impairment leading to mental retardation, brain damage increasing the risk of seizures resulting in residual epilepsy, increased intracranial pressure leading to hydrocephalus, and inflammation of the optic nerve causing visual defects.
